worldcombat.skill.earthquake.summary: Drives its weight into the earth so the whole ground under it heaves up at once: only grounded foes are hit, those caught are hurled upward and shoved out, and the ground is left with radiating cracks that fade. Aftershock trades a lighter main shock for a second tremor shortly after.
worldcombat.skill.earthquake.use.0: Heave every grounded foe standing around you at once
worldcombat.skill.earthquake.use.1: Break a close surround and throw foes off the ground
worldcombat.skill.earthquake.use.2: Skip airborne targets and hit the ones standing
worldcombat.skill.earthquake.use.3: Leave fading cracks to mark the ground just heaved
worldcombat.skill.earthquake.description: The caster must be standing on the ground. When it heaves, each grounded foe in the disc takes about %1$s damage, up to %2$s foes per cast (main shock and aftershock combined). Airborne targets are safe, and the target's defence, type and crit are settled on the hit.
It reaches %1$s blocks; those caught are thrown upward at %2$s blocks/tick and shoved %3$s blocks outward.
It opens a few cracks along the real terrain that then fade; the cracks are only a visual and do not change the ground blocks.
Aftershock on: the main shock is about ×0.86 with wind-up +4 and cooldown +10 ticks, but %1$s s later a half-strength tremor heaves again. It only catches enemies that were airborne during the main shock (for example heaved up) or that entered the smaller disc afterwards: if they have landed and are still inside, they take one hit; any one enemy is struck at most once per cast.
Aftershock off (single shock): the main shock is about ×1.15 and settles at once, with a shorter wind-up and cooldown.
worldcombat.skill.earthquake.timing: After a %1$s s wind-up it spends %3$s PP, then recovers for %2$s s with a %4$s s cooldown.
worldcombat.skill.earthquake.growth.0: At level %1$s the upheaval rises to %2$s, the reach to %3$s blocks, and the launch to %4$s.
On: the main shock is about ×0.86 with a longer wind-up and cooldown, but about a second later a half-strength tremor heaves again to catch whoever was airborne or arrived after the main shock; any one enemy is struck at most once, good against bulky standers and jumpers. Off (single shock): about ×1.15 and settles at once, for fragile foes or when you must stop immediately.
The companion only considers Earthquake when a threat is this close; lower it to heave only at arm's reach, raise it to walk in further first.

At least this many visible, grounded foes standing on the same continuous layer of ground as the caster must be inside the real reach before it heaves (broken ground, ledges and other floors do not count); raise it for surrounded-only use, set it to 1 to heave at a single target. Whether it walks in first is still decided by Consider distance.
